observations: Net gamma exposure is positive at the close: dealers are long gamma and hedge against the direction of price moves
Spot closed just above the zero-gamma level, so the market sits on the long-gamma side of the flip point but only marginally, with the boundary immediately underneath
The call wall sits above spot and the put wall directly below it: the reference levels bracket the close in an unusually narrow band rather than framing a wide range
Gamma coverage of the chain is complete, so the exposure figures are not the product of a partial book
The twenty-five delta put skew is inside GaleCore's calm zone, well under the threshold, and the wing premium over the at-the-money is modest
The volatility index settled in the low teens and the vol-of-vol index is subdued, consistent with an options market that is not pricing an imminent shock
implications: With dealers long gamma, hedging flows should dampen moves and favour mean reversion, so realized volatility is expected to stay contained while the regime holds

Because the flip point is barely below spot, the long-gamma character of hedging flows is fragile: a small downward move would place the market on the other side of it, where the same flows would amplify rather than dampen
With both walls adjacent to spot, the nearest hedging reference on either side is close, so the levels at which dealer flow would be expected to change character are not far away in either direction
A calm skew alongside positive gamma is a coherent combination: the options market is not paying up for protection while hedging flows are counter-cyclical

evidence.claim: Net GEX is positive, dealers are long gamma
Spot is above the zero-gamma level, but only marginally
The call wall sits above spot
The put wall sits directly below spot
Gamma coverage of the chain is complete
The skew level semaphore is in the calm zone
The skew ratio is well under the threshold that would flag it

limitations: Post-session read: GEX is computed at request time after the close, while the volatility and vol-of-vol indices are their afternoon settlement prints
The skew snapshot carries no GaleCore timestamp, so snapshot freshness is UNKNOWN; it reflects the moment of the request
The skew is read from an expiration roughly two months out, not from the front of the curve, so it describes the term where GaleCore measures it and not the immediate tail
GEX reflects current open interest and coverage and will shift with the next session's flow
The gamma regime is a sign classification only; the magnitude relative to total exposure is not validated, and proximity of spot to the flip point is a level reading, not a probability
No comparison with earlier sessions is made here; such comparisons are only valid through the query step
Qualitative statements are not checked for entailment by the validator; only paths, numbers and directives are
